newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Daewoo Motor says Artec buys 26 pct stake.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo Motor says Artec buys 26 pct stake.

text.p: Daewoo Motor Co's managing director Choi Il-sun said on Friday Malaysia's Artec Ltd bought a 26 percent stake in the South Korean carmaker.
Choi contradicted an earlier Daewoo statement that Artec was a subsidiary of the Union Bank of Switzerland. He told Reuters that Artec was a Malaysian investment vehicle.
Choi said: "UBS initially helped Artec to mobilise investors. I think the whole report related to UBS was distorted."
In a statement released earlier on Friday, Daewoo described Artec as a subsidiary of the Swiss bank.
A company spokesman said a corrected statement would be issued shortly.
Choi said he had no information about how Artec had raised its funds.
"I don't know how many members there are or who they are," he said, referring to investors who put up $200 million to buy the third largest stake in South Korea's third largest automaker.
Choi said Artec did not have any management rights in Daewoo. Its investors were hoping to realise a profit from their 18.45 million shares when the company goes public.
Daewoo Motor chairman Kim Tae-gou said earlier this year an initial public offering would be made in 1998 or 1999.
